goal: Build a small React app this weekend, something like a habit tracker with local storage
interpretation: By the end of the weekend, the learner has built and run a working habit tracker in React (Vite) that persists data to localStorage, and understands the hooks and component patterns behind it.
assumptions: The 360 minutes is video viewing time only, so the plan fits about 6 hours of videos with no time reserved for practice.
Learner is comfortable with modern JS (ES6 modules, arrow functions, destructuring, array methods) given 'JavaScript fundamentals', so these are not re-taught.
A habit tracker means adding, completing and deleting habits, with daily or streak tracking and data persisted in localStorage.
Plain JavaScript React is preferred over TypeScript since only JS fundamentals are known.
Functional components and hooks are taught, not legacy class components.

sub_topics.title: React mental model and JSX
sub_topics.why: As a backend engineer who knows JS, they need to learn the declarative UI, components, props and JSX syntax, and how these differ from DOM scripting.

sub_topics.title: Vite project setup and project structure
sub_topics.why: They know npm, so they only need Vite scaffolding, the dev server, file layout and how the entry point mounts the app.

sub_topics.title: Components, props and composition patterns
sub_topics.why: A habit tracker needs a list, items, a form and a header, so they need to split the UI into reusable components and pass data and callbacks down.

sub_topics.title: useState, event handling, controlled forms and rendering lists
sub_topics.why: Adding, toggling and deleting habits requires state updates, controlled inputs, keys and immutable updates to arrays and objects.

sub_topics.title: useEffect and persisting state to localStorage
sub_topics.why: Saving and loading habits needs side effects, dependency arrays, lazy state initialization and JSON serialization, which they already know. A custom useLocalStorage hook is a good fit.

sub_topics.title: Custom hooks, lifting state up and component patterns
sub_topics.why: Structuring the app cleanly means extracting reusable logic and deciding where state lives, a step toward maintainable code.

sub_topics.title: Build a habit tracker app in React end to end
sub_topics.why: A project video that builds a similar app with local storage ties all the concepts together and is the backbone of the plan.

picks.title: React To-Do App Tutorial | Build a Todo List with CRUD in React JS | Frontend Project

Its chapters cover a form component, an array in state rendered with map, delete, UUIDs, useEffect with localStorage persistence and update. That exercises the add, complete, delete and persist workflow the learner needs. Skip the Create React App and Tailwind setup (first 3.5 minutes) and use Vite instead.

picks.title: Save State to LocalStorage & Persist on Refresh with React.js
picks.reason: It focuses on the localStorage mechanics that the larger build glosses over: saving state, how values are stored (storage formats), and hydrating state from storage on refresh. That should help the learner persist and restore habit data correctly, including serializing objects.

evidence.quote: Learn how to save React state and load it when a page refreshes using localStorage.
We'll learn how to set up a simple example using React state, using an onClick handler to update that state, and using localStorage to store and retrieve the value.

picks.confidence_note: The description and chapters look relevant but are unverified. It may use a lazy initial state pattern rather than useEffect for loading.

picks.title: Build a Complete To-Do List App with React + Vite | Dashboard, Reminders & Local Storage Tutorial
picks.reason: A React + Vite build that, per the description, creates a custom useLocalStorage hook and uses it across a task app with add, edit, delete, complete and filtering. It is a good capstone for extracting the persistence logic into a reusable hook and for seeing a Vite-based component architecture, which the learner can adapt to a habit tracker.

evidence.quote: In this comprehensive tutorial, we'll create a feature-rich task management app with a modern dashboard, reminder notifications, and persistent storage.

picks.confidence_note: There is no transcript, so everything comes from the description. The teaching depth and the coverage of lifting state up are unverified. It also uses Tailwind and extra features (reminders, dashboard) beyond the need.

warnings: Every candidate was assessed from chapters or descriptions only, with no transcripts. All confidence scores are therefore low to moderate, and the teaching depth of every pick is unverified.

The plan uses about 162 of 360 minutes (about 45%). The remaining candidates were redundant, TypeScript-based, too advanced, or dependent on missing series parts, so I left the time unfilled rather than pad it. Use the spare time to build the app yourself.

No video in the pool builds a habit tracker in plain React + Vite. The build step relies on todo apps (fsyfL33soRQ and X92kk5iT8CM), so you will add habit-specific features yourself: daily completion, streaks and a per-habit history.

fsyfL33soRQ uses Create React App (outdated tooling) and Tailwind. Follow its component, state and effect logic but use the Vite project you create from the Vite segment. X92kk5iT8CM also uses Tailwind and Vite, so expect some extra styling setup.

Lifting state up and component composition patterns are only weakly covered. They are likely touched in the Tech With Tim segment and the two todo builds, but this could not be verified. Consider the React docs section on sharing state between components.
The Vite coverage rests on the crash course's first project chapter, and the Tech With Tim template walkthrough may overlap with it. Skip whichever setup you have already done.
I assumed plain JavaScript React is preferred, so TypeScript-based builds were excluded.
